heroHeadline: CRS-34 Third Launch Attempt Today (May 15, 6:05 p.m. EDT) After Two Weather Scrubs; SpaceX IPO Public S-1 Filing Window Opens Today
heroSubtitle: 8,775 days of SpaceX milestones — After two consecutive weather scrubs on May 12 (T-4 min abort) and May 13 (T-30s abort) at Cape Canaveral SLC-40, SpaceX and NASA retargeted CRS-34 Cargo Dragon for a third launch attempt on May 15, 2026, at 6:05 p.m. EDT. Booster B1096 (6th flight) targets LZ-40 RTLS recovery; Dragon C209 carries ~6,500 lbs of Expedition 74 science experiments and crew supplies, with ISS Harmony docking now targeting ~7:00 a.m. EDT on May 17. A successful CRS-34 launch will be SpaceX's 58th orbital mission of 2026 and the 611th cumulative Falcon booster recovery. Simultaneously, May 15 opens the earliest possible window for SpaceX to publicly file its IPO S-1 registration statement (confidential draft filed April 1 as 'Project Apex') — a $75B raise at $1.75T+ valuation targeting June Nasdaq debut would be the largest U.S. IPO in history. IFT-12 Starship Block 3 remains firmly on track for NET May 19 (5:30 p.m. CDT, OLP-2, Starbase, Booster 19 + Ship 39 V3), with pre-flight checkout milestones completed and FAA flight safety approval in hand. SpaceX: 57 orbital missions in 2026, 610 total booster recoveries, 11 Starship integrated flight tests to date, 10,374+ Starlink satellites in orbit, 10M+ subscribers.
